results.title: Miscalculation in production shakes the world's copper giant - upi.com
results.content: # Miscalculation in production shakes the world's copper giant. Codelco, Chile's state-owned mining company and the world’s largest copper producer, is facing mounting scrutiny after discovering an overestimation in production figures. May 26 (UPI) -- Codelco, Chile's state-owned mining company and the world's largest copper producer, is facing mounting scrutiny after discovering an overestimation of more than 27,000 metric tons in its production figures, triggering executive departures, a criminal complaint and tensions with labor unions. Following an internal audit, Codelco acknowledged that its previously reported 2025 production figure of 1,334,445 metric tons of fine copper was inaccurate because it included 26,875 metric tons produced at the beginning of 2026. As a result, more than 6,000 Codelco workers may be required to return part of the production bonuses they received after meeting company targets. "When a company that is 100% owned by the Chilean state delivers figures that later need correction, it weakens the perception of Chile as a predictable and rigorous mining jurisdiction," Viera said.

results.content: # GoldMining starts exploration drilling at Colombia’s Yarumalito project. The Yarumalito project lies in the Mid Cauca belt, around 105km from Medellín and 40km south of La Mina. GoldMining has commenced an exploration drilling programme at its wholly owned Yarumalito Gold-Copper Project in Colombia’s Antioquia region. The Yarumalito site is situated in the Mid Cauca gold-copper belt, approximately 105km south-southwest of Medellín and about 40km south of the company’s La Mina project. The drilling will focus on sections of the P-1 porphyry unit that have received less exploration, as this area is believed to hold significant gold-copper mineralisation. GoldMining president and CEO Alastair Still said: “Yarumalito sits in the heart of Colombia’s prolific Mid Cauca belt, in close proximity to major discoveries like Collective Mining’s Guayabales project and Aris Mining’s Marmato mine. “With diamond core drilling now underway on our second active exploration drilling programme in the Americas for 2026, we are testing a newly refined geological model at Yarumalito.

results.content: # More Homes, More Price Cuts: Realtor.com Sees Market Conditions Improving For Buyers. Homebuyers are seeing more inventory, moderating prices and longer time on market this spring, but affordability challenges and renewed mortgage rate volatility continue to weigh on the housing market, according to a new report from Realtor.com. The company's spring 2026 housing market progress report found active listings continued to rise nationwide this year, extending a multi-year recovery in inventory levels from pandemic-era lows. Nationally, active listings in April rose 9.3% year over year in the Northeast and 11.5% in the Midwest, while inventory gains in the South slowed to 1.8%, according to Realtor.com data. The findings reinforce broader housing trends seen this spring, as rising inventory and moderating prices gradually create a more balanced market environment despite continued affordability pressure. results.title: The Rise of South America's Copper Corridor - AZoMining
results.content: Image 2: An AZoNetwork Site. **South America has long been the world's most consequential copper-producing region, but a new chapter in that story is now unfolding. Chile, Peru, and Argentina together hold vast Andean copper reserves, and their combined trajectory is drawing unprecedented capital from the world's largest mining companies, giving rise to what is being termed a "copper corridor.”**. South America will play a vital role in meeting this challenge, as it currently contributes around 41% of the world's copper output.1-3. Peru contributes high-grade deposits with copper concentrations ranging from 1.2% to 2.5% and has a rapidly growing portfolio of 84 active exploration projects. Argentina adds value with the highest ore grades in the region, averaging 1.5% to 2.8% copper, and a geological frontier that remains largely unexplored.4,5. Industry projections point to a combined output target of 11 to 14 million tonnes by 2035, which could push the corridor's global market share to between 35% and 40%.

results.title: Codelco Restores Normal Operations Following Antofagasta Earthquake - Discovery Alert
results.content: ## Seismic Risk and the Copper Supply Chain: What the Antofagasta Earthquake Reveals. The global copper market operates with a structural vulnerability that rarely appears in quarterly earnings reports or commodity outlooks: a significant portion of the world's copper supply sits on one of the most seismically active stretches of the planet's crust. Understanding how mining operators manage this reality — and what happens when the earth moves beneath their operations — offers a sharper lens on supply chain resilience than most conventional market analysis provides. Chile's Antofagasta region, which contributes a disproportionately large share of the country's total copper output, experiences seismic activity on a recurring basis. A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Antofagasta region on a Monday afternoon, with its epicentre located approximately **31 kilometres east of Calama**, the urban centre that functions as the logistical hub for several major copper mining operations in the area.

results.title: Mobilint Nears Mass Production of Second-Generation NPU 'Regulus' - thelec.net
results.content: Mobilint Nears Mass Production of Second-Generation NPU 'Regulus'. ## Company Completed Recent Single-Run Production, Plans USB AI Product Launch at Computex. Mobilint is approaching mass production of its second-generation neural processing unit (NPU) Regulus, industry sources said on May 26. The company recently completed a single-run production process for the chip, according to the sources. Single-run production refers to a small-volume manufacturing stage conducted immediately before full-scale mass production for customer qualification and verification. Industry observers said the completion of single-run production suggests that Regulus passed initial customer evaluations conducted on MPW prototype samples. Some in the industry expect Regulus mass production to begin earlier than Mobilint's original second-half target, with optimistic forecasts pointing to June. Mobilint has already secured purchase orders for Regulus from customers including Daon I&C, according to industry sources. Mobilint plans to unveil a USB-based Regulus product at Computex 2026, which will be held in Taipei from June 2 to June 5.
